books.name: Yesterday
books.focus: played · went · ate · was · didn't · Did…?

items.a: I play in the park every day.
items.tip: Regular verbs add -ed in the past: play → played.
items.say: Yesterday I played in the park.

items.a: We go to the beach on Sundays.
items.b: Last Sunday we ___ to the beach.
items.tip: go is irregular: go → went.
items.say: Last Sunday we went to the beach.

items.a: Mia eats a big cake.
items.tip: eat is irregular: eat → ate.
items.say: Yesterday Mia ate a big cake.

items.a: The dragon is very tired.
items.b: Last night the dragon ___ very tired.
items.tip: is → was in the past (I/he/she/it was).
items.say: Last night the dragon was very tired.

items.a: They are at the zoo.
items.tip: are → were in the past (you/we/they were).
items.say: Yesterday they were at the zoo.

items.a: I don't see the bus.
items.tip: In past negatives, didn't + the base verb: I didn't see (not didn't saw).
items.say: Yesterday I didn't see the bus.

items.a: Do you like the film?
items.tip: Past questions start with Did + base verb: Did you like the film?
items.say: Did you like the film last night?

items.a: Ben buys a new kite.
items.b: Last week Ben ___ a new kite.
items.tip: buy is irregular: buy → bought.
items.say: Last week Ben bought a new kite.

books.name: Bigger and Best
books.focus: taller than · not as fast as · the highest

items.a: Tom is shorter than Ana.
items.tip: Short words add -er + than: tall → taller than.
items.say: Ana is taller than Tom.

items.a: The red car is not as fast as the blue car.
items.cue: Now say it about the blue car.
items.b: The blue car is ___ the red car.
items.tip: not as fast as ↔ faster than (the other way round).
items.say: The blue car is faster than the red car.

items.a: No mountain is higher than Mount Everest.
items.b: Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
items.tip: The superlative: the + adjective + -est: the highest.
items.say: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

items.a: This puzzle is easier than that one.
items.cue: Now say it about that puzzle.
items.tip: Long adjectives use more + adjective + than: more difficult than.
items.say: That puzzle is more difficult than this one.

items.a: Lily sings better than me.
items.tip: not as well as = worse than. sing well → as well as (well, not good, with a verb).
items.say: I don't sing as well as Lily.

items.a: Pip's house is the smallest in the street.
items.cue: Now say it about the other houses.
items.b: All the other houses are ___ Pip's house.
items.tip: If Pip's house is the smallest, the others are bigger than it. big → bigger (double g).
items.say: All the other houses are bigger than Pip's house.

items.a: The film was more exciting than the book.
items.cue: Now say it about the book.
items.tip: more exciting than ↔ less exciting than (or not as exciting as).
items.say: The book was less exciting than the film.

items.a: Nobody in our class is funnier than Max.
items.b: Max is ___ person in our class.
items.tip: funny → the funniest (y changes to i).
items.say: Max is the funniest person in our class.

books.name: Plans and Rules
books.focus: going to · have to · can't · don't have to · 's

items.a: My plan is to visit Grandma on Saturday.
items.tip: For plans we use be going to + verb: I'm going to visit Grandma.
items.say: I'm going to visit Grandma on Saturday.

items.a: It's important to wear a helmet.
items.tip: For rules we say have to or must + verb: You have to wear a helmet.
items.say: You have to wear a helmet.

items.a: This book belongs to my brother.
items.tip: To show who owns something, add 's: my brother's book.
items.say: This is my brother's book.

items.a: Swimming in this lake is not allowed.
items.tip: When something is not allowed we say can't or mustn't: You can't swim here.
items.say: You can't swim in this lake.

items.a: Let's have a picnic!
items.tip: Why don't we…? is a friendly way to suggest something.
items.say: Why don't we have a picnic?

items.a: Our flat has two bedrooms.
items.b: There ___ two bedrooms in our flat.
items.tip: For more than one thing: There are two bedrooms.
items.say: There are two bedrooms in our flat.

items.a: It isn't necessary to bring lunch.
items.tip: don't have to = it isn't necessary (you can if you want). mustn't means it is not allowed!
items.say: You don't have to bring lunch.

items.a: I started learning the piano two years ago.
items.b: I ___ the piano for two years.
items.tip: Something that started in the past and is still true: have + past participle + for: I have learned the piano for two years.
items.say: I have learned the piano for two years.
